newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan plans five-nation meeting on Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan plans five-nation meeting on Afghanistan.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday it was planning a five-nation conference to discuss ways to resolve the conflict in neighbouring Afghanistan.
Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan told a news conference that the planned meeting would involve Afghanistan's immediate neighbours -- Iran, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.
Khan said the United States and Russia might be invited to the conference as observers.
He said Pakistan was also trying to hold an intra-Afghan dialogue under U.N. auspices with the aim of having a broad-based government in the war-shattered country.

Pakistan recognised the government of the Taleban Islamic movement in Afghanistan last month and is accused by opposition factions of helping the mainly ethnic Pashtun Taleban militia, which controls more than two-thirds of the country.
Pakistan denies the charge, and Khan said all ethnic groups should take part in the intra-Afghan dialogue "so that a broad-based government is formed".
